note: Not a real key. A constant, so a consumer can prove it round-trips this exact shape. Every field is 32 bytes because that is what @fetchproxy/protocol's generateX25519 and generateEd25519 return (both slice(-32) the pkcs8 export). The byte patterns are chosen so the encoded forms contain BOTH '+' and '/': a vector of uniform bytes encodes without either, and so cannot tell standard base64 from base64url — which is a difference this format cares about, since fetchproxy reads these with atob().
